implementation_notes: Scala/Akka deserves specific mention because Akka Cluster is the framework feature that makes microservices sprawl feel justified — nodes, sharding and cluster membership make a fleet of small services look architecturally rigorous while adding discovery, gossip and eventual-consistency failure modes that nothing else in the estate has. It is a case where the pattern is genuinely useful at a scale where most teams are not, and where using it below that scale produces operational load with none of the benefit. The consolidation is one JVM with one sbt project containing several modules, keeping the internal boundaries explicit.
idiom_name: Akka Cluster per capability; sbt module per domain noun
pitfalls: Akka Cluster below the scale it was designed for adds gossip and rebalancing cost with none of the benefit.
One sbt module per domain noun makes the module boundary and the deploy boundary the same by default.
Serialization formats per service mean a shared domain change is N compatibility problems, and Scala's case class serialization is implicit.
